item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q002_mazg_hise_remote_homology","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, d1vmga_ (a.204.1.2; MazG-like family, sunid 116993) and d1y6xa1 (a.204.1.4; HisE-like/PRA-PH family, sunid 140797) are in different families but the same all-alpha NTP pyrophosphatases superfamily (a.204.1, sunid 101386). This supports remote homology—a probable common evolutionary ancestor—rather than close, family-level homology; their shared all-alpha NTP pyrophosphatase fold/class alone would be weaker structural evidence, but their shared superfamily is the relevant evolutionary assignment. SCOPe identifies the d1y6xa1 protein as phosphoribosyl-ATP pyrophosphatase HisE, whereas the d1vmga_ protein is annotated as hypothetical despite its MazG-like family placement. Therefore, transferring HisE activity, phosphoribosyl-ATP substrate specificity, histidine-biosynthesis pathway membership, or catalytic residues to d1vmga_ would exceed the classification evidence. Likewise, MazG-specific substrate preferences or physiological roles should not be assigned to d1y6xa1. Either domain may be a remote structural template for the common core, but active-site and functional modeling require corroborating sequence conservation, catalytic/ligand geometry, biochemical assays, and genomic or pathway context.","evidence_used":["/api/v1/","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d1vmga_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d1y6xa1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/113676","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/122676","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/116995","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/140801","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/116994","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/140798","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/116993","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/140797","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/101386","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/101385","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/46456"]}]}
